children: Anil Agarwal-led Vedanta Power will be included in the Nifty 500 and Nifty Smallcap 250 indices from September 30. The company was recently listed on the exchanges following its demerger from Vedanta.

The changes will come into effect after the close of trading on September 29. With its inclusion in the Nifty Smallcap 250, Vedanta Power will also become part of the Nifty MidSmallcap 400 and Nifty Smallcap 500 indices.

The inclusion will expand the company’s representation across widely tracked market benchmarks. However, index inclusion does not automatically translate into additional fund flows or a valuation re-rating, said an analyst.

The development comes as Vedanta Power embarks on an aggressive capacity expansion programme. The company currently has about 5 GW of operational generation capacity and expects to add about 600 MW by the end of FY27. It is targeting 12 GW by FY33, implying nearly a three-fold expansion from its FY26 operational base. The company has also outlined a longer-term ambition of reaching 20 GW.

Vedanta Power operates the Talwandi Sabo Thermal Power Plant, Sakti Thermal Power Plant, Meenakshi Energy and Jharsuguda Thermal Power Plant. About 85 per cent of its capacity is backed by long-term domestic coal linkages, providing greater visibility on fuel availability.

The expansion plans come amid rising electricity demand from manufacturing, infrastructure, data centres, electric mobility and urbanisation. While renewable energy capacity continues to grow, thermal generation remains an important source of dispatchable power for the grid.

Vedanta Power is also pursuing sustainability measures. Biomass co-firing at its Talwandi Sabo plant has crossed 5 per cent of fuel consumption. The company has outlined targets to reduce greenhouse-gas intensity and improve water efficiency, with an objective of achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 or earlier.

title: Vedanta Power to join Nifty 500, Smallcap 250
